title: Harmon label registry
description: Machine-readable source of truth for every GitHub label family this repository knows about. Rendered into provisioning (setup-github-labels.sh), the docs taxonomy table, and skill behavior (the writers field is the triage write-allowlist). Mixed namespaces (foreman:*) are split into separately modeled families sharing a prefix, so `source` stays family-level; writers/lifecycle/color/arming still override per value.

writer.description: human = anyone with triage access; trusted-human = an actor-verifying consumer additionally authenticates the applier (the label still carries no permission — the class names which consumer-side check applies); agent = an AI agent may write it (the triage skill's allowlist reads exactly this); tool:<name> = written only by that tool's own machinery.

lifecycle.description: durable = stays on the issue once true; transient = removed as soon as the state clears; claim-release = added at claim, removed at release; tool-managed = the owning tool applies and removes it.

value.description: The part after `<prefix>:`, or the complete label name when the family's prefix is null (which is how names outside the family:value convention, like `autorelease: pending`, are modeled).

provision.description: Per-value off switch (only false is legal): the value belongs to the family's semantics but is never seeded — e.g. work types GitHub already ships at repo creation. A family-off has no per-value on switch.

prefix.description: Label-name prefix (`area` renders `area:<value>`); null for families of bare label names.

axis.description: Which question the family answers. classification = area/domain/layer (at most one each); strategy = advisory execution/routing axes; model = the suggest/claim agent vocabulary; foreman = arming inputs and lifecycle outputs; release/meta = tool and platform namespaces.

source.description: inline = values enumerated here; agent-registry = values rendered from agent-registry.json (values must be empty here); tool-owned = the consuming tool creates the labels on demand and provisioning leaves them alone.

registry_set.description: Which agent-registry render feeds a source: agent-registry family.

exclusive.description: True when an issue should carry at most one value of the family (the classification axes). Advisory families whose conflicts have a defined resolution (tier strongest-wins, method rank) are not exclusive.

provision.description: True when `task setup:github-labels` seeds the family. Tool-owned and retired families are never provisioned.

gate.description: The family exists only where the named opt-in is active: provisioning includes it only under the matching renderer flag (--foreman / --release-please), and the generated docs wrap or drop its rows per profile. Applies to non-provisioned families too — a tool-owned family whose tool ships behind the opt-in is gated the same way.

retired.description: Legacy family: never provisioned, rendered as retired in docs. Provisioning is additive-only, so live labels survive until an operator re-maps and deletes them by hand (`gh label edit --name` preserves issue associations).

open_values.description: The family legitimately has un-enumerated members (created on demand); placeholder names the docs rendering.
